sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with common-law-inspired commercial and maritime statutes and a unitary national regulatory framework
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Central America Association Agreement as applied to Panama

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on AML/CFT (adopting FATF Recommendations); Ley No. 70 de 14 de marzo de 2019 establishing the beneficial ownership transparency regime; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 429 de 2019 and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 129 de 2020 regulating UBO registration and access; together with regulations of the Superintendencia de Bancos and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence on the settlor, foundation council, protector, beneficiaries, and any attorney-in-fact. All parties must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, UAF national designations, and reputable adverse-media/PEP databases. The initial endowment and source of funds must be documented. For this medium-risk maritime towage and salvage scope, a jurisdiction with non-transparent ownership chain above 25% triggers escalation to the resident agent's compliance committee, and any PEP match requires senior management approval and UAF notification as applicable under Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Portal de Servicios Electrónicos (www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All formal registration filings must be in Spanish. The foundation must adopt a denomination in Latin script; non-Latin-script names must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish and accompanied by a certified translation. A secondary English-language commercial style may be registered as a trade denomination so long as the legal name remains in Spanish.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects the proposed foundation name, the petitioner may file a written 'recurso de reconsideración' before the Dirección General of the Registro Público within five business days of notice. The submission must include the original search certificate, the rejected name, corrected alternatives, and any trademark or trade-name evidence establishing priority. Where the reconsideration is denied, the petitioner may pursue the appellate administrative remedy under Ley 38 de 2001 and thereafter appeal to the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Panama.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only to the extent that a physical Panamanian registered office is maintained at the licensed resident agent's address. For this deep-sea towage and emergency salvage operation, a purely virtual address is insufficient commercial substance for tax purposes; the foundation should document its maritime employment contracts, vessel ownership or charter, invoicing, crew/management, and escrow/settlement procedures in Panama or through demonstrable outsourced operating arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low during pre-incorporation (approx. 5% annualized probability absent adverse risk signals); increases to approximately 20-30% once the entity is active, particularly if registered with the Autoridad Marítima de Panamá, engages in Panamanian territorial waters, or triggers DGI tax verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley No. 25 de 2018; Articles 9 (minimum capital), 16-17 (registered office and resident agent), 19-21 (registration), and 26-30 (Foundation Council governance).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundacion de Interes Privado (Foundation Charter) together with the Reglamento (Foundation Regulations); recorded under the Foundation's electronic file (Folio Electronico).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum foundation capital of USD 10,000.00 under Law 25 of 1995, Article 9, which may be satisfied in cash or assets of equivalent value; no statutory escrow deposit is required, but the contributed assets must be identified in the Charter or Regulations and recorded in the foundation accounts, and the stated capital must be reflected in the registered Charter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL NO. 1-2025. The Foundation Council of [Foundation Name], by unanimous written consent, resolves: 1. Acceptance of Foundation Capital: The Founder's declaration establishing a Foundation Capital of USD 10,000.00 is accepted, and the contributed initial assets are recorded as fully satisfying the minimum capital requirement of Law 25 of 1995. 2. Registered Office and Agent: The registered office is established at [Registered Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the Resident Agent, [Law Firm], is appointed as required by Law 25 of 1995. 3. Officers: [Founder] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Secretary of the Foundation Council, each authorized to direct the Foundation's bank accounts and towage and salvage contracts. Adopted this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Online Name Reservation Portal and Ventanilla Unica de Nombres
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative foundation names in Spanish through the Public Registry's online reservation system or in person; the Registry searches its database for identical or phonetically confusing names and reserves the approved name for a statutory period. Pay the nominal name-search fee and obtain the printed name-availability certification to attach to the Charter.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Letter of instruction from founder or resident agent
Copy of founder's passport or ID
List of three proposed names in Spanish
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, immediately file a new set of three alternate names with the same application; if the reservation expires, pay the renewed filing fee and re-submit. A formal refusal may be appealed to the Director General of the Public Registry within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaria Publica authorized by the Corte Suprema de Justicia de Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder or its corporate representative appears before a Panamanian notary to execute the Acta Constitutiva and the Reglamento, both in Spanish. The resident agent must be named and its acceptance obtained. If the founder is a foreign entity, produce certified corporate resolutions and notarized translations; the notary then issues the original testimonio (certified first copy).
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter and Regulations
Passport or corporate documents of the founder
Certificate of name reservation from the Public Registry
Acceptance letter of the Resident Agent
Consent of registered office address provider
Certified Spanish translation of any foreign-language documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects, file corrected pages before execution; if the notary refuses protocolization due to incomplete resident agent consent, obtain the missing consent and re-execute the instrument within the same day or next business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial testimonio and a duplicate authenticated copy with the Private Interest Foundations Section, together with proof of payment of the B/.350.00 statutory registration fee, and submit the resident agent's sworn acceptance. The Registry examines the Charter against Law 25 of 1995 and, upon approval, assigns the foundation's electronic file and records the foundation with a registration date and number.
required_dossiers: Notarial written consent (testimonio de la escritura publica)
Authenticated duplicate of the Foundation Charter
Reglamento, if not incorporated into the Charter
Resident agent acceptance letter
Proof of payment of the statutory registration fee
Name reservation certificate
Filing form of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice (prevencion), counsel must cure the stated defects within the granted term, usually two to three business days, by filing an aclaracion or amended page; if registration is refused on substantive grounds, file a reconsideration motion with the Director General within five business days and a subsequent appeal to the Sala Cuarta of the Corte Suprema de Justicia if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registro de Fundacion Extract and Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Certification Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registration entry is completed, request the certified extract (extracto de la fundacion) and the certificate of registration from the certification window or the online platform. This instrument is used for opening bank accounts, obtaining the RUC, and presenting to the Autoridad Maritima de Panama for licensing.
required_dossiers: Registry filing receipt
Application letter requesting the certified extract
Payment of certification fee
Registered Charter reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the extract contains discrepancies against the Charter, submit a written correction request with the notarial copy; if the certification is delayed, escalate to the Seccion de Atencion al Usuario of the Public Registry and request expedition under the Registry's customer service standard.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) - Sede Electronica and Regional Administration, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Unico de Contribuyente (RUC) application with the DGI using the certified Registry extract, identify the foundation's economic activity as maritime towage and salvage auxiliary services, and obtain the RUC number together with the digital tax signature. Register as an employer for the issuance of payroll certificates as part of the same filing.
required_dossiers: Certified foundation extract from the Public Registry
Foundation Charter and Regulations
Resident agent power of attorney
Identity documents of foundation council members
RUC application form
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the economic activity classification or the foundation's documentation, file a written correction of the application within five business days; if the RUC is denied, present a reconsideration petition before the DGI National Directorate, with the foundation extract and Charter as supporting evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldia de Panama - Direccion de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal Aviso de Operacion (and, where applicable, the business license) by presenting the RUC and the certified foundation extract, and classify the activity as maritime auxiliary services. Pay the proportional municipal surface tax for the first operating year and obtain the municipal certificate of operation for the registered office and the towage operations office.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certified foundation extract
Lease agreement or ownership title of the registered office
Completed Aviso de Operacion form
Fire safety clearance (for the office premises, if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal treasury questions the declared area or activity, file the rectification form with supporting lease and plan documents within five business days; a denial may be appealed to the Alcalde or its designee under the Ley 106 de 1973 and the municipality's rental regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Maritima de Panama (AMP) - Direccion General de Marina Mercante, Direccion de Servicios Auxiliares Maritimos
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Operacion para Servicios Auxiliares Maritimos - Remolque de Altura y Salvamento (Maritime Auxiliary Services Operating Permit for Deep-Sea Towage and Salvor Companies)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Direccion Nacional de Evaluacion y Seguimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Moderate Impact: Environmental Impact Assessment (EsIA) registration and filing required for the shore base, tug berthing, and maintenance facilities associated with offshore towage and salvage operations under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 7 de agosto de 2009 and its modifications; Category III does not apply to auxiliary maritime services of this type.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annex I (oil), Annex IV (sewage), and Annex VI (NOx, SOx, and VOCs); Panama flag vessel annual inspection by AMP; ballast water management per the BWM Convention; bilge water and oily waste must be discharged only at AMP-authorized reception facilities; fuel sulfur shall not exceed 0.50% m/m outside emission control areas and 0.10% m/m within designated ECA zones; onboard waste handling and garbage logs required under MiAMBIENTE and AMP resolutions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and occupancy clearance from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama for shore offices, tug berths, and workshops; structural and load inspection of quayside equipment and davits; workplace occupational health and safety program registered with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); and emergency response and spill-containment plan filed with the Sistema Nacional de Proteccion Civil (SINAPROC) for shore installations and vessel operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas), Republic of Panama; official e-filing and taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first register its foundation charter with the Registro Público de Panamá and appoint a resident agent with a Panamanian registered address. The resident agent then files the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) application through the Sede Electrónica DGI, submitting the notarized foundation deed, public registry certificate, resolution appointing foundation officers, notarized passport copies of the founder and council members, and the Aviso de Operación obtained from the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) when the PIF directly engages in commercial maritime activities. The DGI issues a single RUC number that serves simultaneously as the income tax TIN and the ITBMS (VAT) registration identifier. Non-resident entities without a fixed establishment in Panama obtain a non-resident RUC (RUC-NE) and must designate a local fiscal representative for service of process and tax notifications; maritime towage and salvage operations additionally require registration with the Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP) and, for customs purposes, enrollment in the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) exporter registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election in the style of the U.S. or the OECD Pillar Two rules. However, under Law 25 of 1995 the founder may elect in the foundation charter whether the PIF's beneficiary rights are irrevocable or revocable and whether the foundation is governed by trust-like asset-partitioning provisions, which informs its civil and tax characterization. For Panamanian tax purposes, an electing PIF providing eligible offshore towage and salvage services may apply the Special Maritime Services Regime established under Law 63 of 2007, administered by AMP, and may also elect the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying headquarters services. Pursuant to Law 254 of 2021, small enterprises with annual gross revenue not exceeding B/. 200,000 may elect the Simplified Regime (Régimen Simplificado) on the Sede Electrónica before the start of the fiscal year, substituting ordinary income tax and full ITBMS compliance with a single-rate turnover tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (Balboas/U.S. dollars) in annual gross turnover is the historical small-taxpayer exemption threshold; under Law 254 of 2021, economic operators with annual gross revenue of up to B/. 200,000 are eligible for the Simplified Regime with reduced ITBMS compliance, while operators with annual gross revenue exceeding B/. 200,000 are mandatorily subject to full regular ITBMS registration as a registered taxable person (sujeto pasivo) regardless of legal form.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for registered ITBMS taxpayers pursuant to Law 254 of 2021 and the implementing DGI regulations in force (Resolution DGI-201-0246 of 2020 and subsequent amendments). Invoices must be issued through a DGI-certified electronic invoicing system using a valid AIG-issued digital certificate (X.509) and transmitted in real time to the DGI's Facturación Electrónica clearance platform via a documented web-service API (SOAP/REST) with XML schema validation. Each invoice receives a unique electronic acceptance code (código de aceptación) and a digital stamp, and must display a QR code for the ANA and DGI audit interoperability; legacy fiscal printers (impresoras fiscales) are tolerated only for certain small taxpayers during the approved transition windows.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% ITBMS is available for exports of tangible goods physically removed from Panama and for export services under Article 1058-A of the Código Fiscal as developed by Law 30 of 2012. Deep-sea towage and emergency salvage services supplied to foreign-flag or internationally trading vessels are treated as zero-rated service exports when the service is deemed performed outside Panamanian territorial waters or where the beneficial use and economic consumption occurs outside Panama, and where the vessel is engaged in international navigation. The service provider must substantiate the cross-border nature via a DGI-approved service-export classification (acuse de exportación de servicios) obtained through the Sede Electrónica before invoicing at 0%; towage in Panamanian internal waters or in connection with port or Canal assistance may instead be outside the zero-rating scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (Formulario Único de Exportación) filed with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the VUCE single-window for foreign trade
Conocimiento de Embarque (Bill of Lading) or ocean/sea waybill evidencing carriage to a foreign port or an international voyage
Certificado de Remesa de Divisas (Inward Remittance Certificate) issued by the receiving Panamanian bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds into Panama's financial system
Contrato de Remolque/Salvamento (towage or salvage contract), including the Lloyds Open Form (LOF) for wreck-removal and marine salvage engagements
Certificado de Registro de Buque (Vessel Registration Certificate) confirming the flag and international trading status of the vessel serviced
Factura Comercial de Exportación (commercial export invoice) with the corresponding packing list and the DGI export-stamped electronic invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to a statutory audit window of five years from the filing date. Where the DGI determines that zero-rating was improperly claimed, it issues a retroactive assessment for the omitted ITBMS plus statutory interest at the legal rate of 10% per annum from the original due date and applies fines of two to five times the tax evaded under Article 1232 of the Código Fiscal, as amended by Law 254 of 2021, with a maximum surcharge of up to 200% of the assessed tax. Fraudulent export zero-rating or VAT-refund claims exceeding B/. 30,000 constitute the criminal offense of tax fraud under Law 70 of 2019, punishable by four to ten years of imprisonment, disqualification from the exporter and e-invoicing registries, and the revocation of ANA customs clearance privileges and maritime operating licenses issued by AMP.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank. Financial supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) is the AML/CFT financial intelligence unit, and Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent for the Republic.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized: the U.S. dollar is legal tender. There are no exchange-control restrictions on current or capital account transactions. Capital and profits may be freely repatriated. Panama applies a territorial tax system, taxing only Panamanian-source income; foreign-source towage and salvage income earned by a Private Interest Foundation is generally outside Panamanian tax unless it involves Panama-source activities. Remittances of profits require documentary support but do not require exchange-control approval or forced conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules or mandatory conversion ratios apply to export proceeds. Because Panama is dollarized and has no central exchange-control bureaucracy, salvage and towage fee receivables may be retained in any currency at any licensed financial institution. Only the UAF cash/negotiable-instrument disclosure threshold (USD 10,000 or equivalent when physically imported or exported) must be observed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium. Foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are not passportable into Panama and cannot act as licensed deposit-taking institutions. An offshore EMI may only serve as an auxiliary payment channel through a Panamanian intermediary bank account, but it cannot provide a standalone Panamanian treasury-clearing rail. For a Private Interest Foundation engaged in offshore towage and salvage, a fully licensed SBP-regulated commercial bank is the only robust and legally defensible clearing route.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for medium-risk offshore PIF structures. At least one Foundation Council member and the ultimate beneficial owner must either appear in person before a Panamanian bank compliance officer or execute a notarized identity-verification protocol before a Panamanian notary and licensed legal counsel. Remote onboarding is only accepted on an exception basis for low-risk clients after enhanced compliance sign-off. For the maritime salvage and towage sector, a physical director visit is strongly recommended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation secrecy veil with a nominee foundation council.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation charter issued under Panama Law 25 of 1995, registered-agent certificate, registry of beneficiaries, foundation council resolution appointing operational authority, notarized and apostilled identification documents for each director, sworn source-of-funds statement, and an organizational ownership chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Maritime salvage and towage invoicing to vessel owners registered in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed towage/salvage contracts, appendices incorporating Lloyd's Open Form or equivalent terms, AIS tracking extracts, master's incident and service reports, P&I insurance certificates, official vessel registry certificates, invoicing files, and a clear no-cash-acceptance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow disbursements to unidentified counterparties or complex multi-party payment flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow/trust agreement, full KYC/AML due-diligence pack on each counterparty, corporate registers and beneficial-ownership documentation, independent sanctions and adverse-media screening reports, and a written purpose-of-disbursement narrative for each escrow schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests to move funds via non-bank channels, virtual-asset platforms, or unregulated money services businesses.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate policy expressly prohibiting virtual-asset and unregulated DSP payment rails, a documented commitment to bank-to-bank SWIFT-only transfers, audited or original bank statements for the preceding fiscal period, a legal opinion on the foreign-source and tax-neutral character of foundation earnings, and updated AML/KYC compliance policies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound injection is executed by USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the founding contributor's bank. Payment narrative must state 'Private Interest Foundation capital contribution' or 'working capital funding' and provide the foundation council resolution authorizing the injection, source-of-wealth evidence, and the contributor's completed KYC documentation. No Panamanian exchange permit is required; the receiving bank's AML system will apply threshold-based UAF reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade, towage, and salvage settlement use bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 wires. Letters of credit are available through MT700 (issue), MT707 (amendment), and MT710 (advice of a third bank) where contractual terms require documentary credit. USD clearing runs over U.S. correspondent networks (Fedwire/CHIPS) and Panama's local clearing switch for same-day domestic transfers. Each outward payment must state a transparent purpose narrative, such as 'Marine towage and salvage services under contract No. ___'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla currency forwards on EUR/GBP/JPY receivable streams arising from international salvage contracts
Cross-currency swaps with SBP-licensed banks for long-term multi-currency treasury matching
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged through an internationally licensed correspondent bank for peripheral currencies lacking deliverable local markets
Over-the-counter currency options written by a securities firm regulated under Panama Law 67 of 2011

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax Payment (Impuesto Anual de Franquicia de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; credited directly to the National Treasury through authorized banking channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 31 covering the preceding calendar year ended December 31; single lump-sum payment with no instalment or extension regime. Fee tier is determined by registered foundation capital: USD 300 (capital up to USD 10,000), USD 400 (up to USD 100,000), USD 500 (up to USD 500,000), USD 800 (over USD 500,000).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after January 31 triggers a 10% surcharge plus 1% monthly interest under Law 25 of 1995, Article 42; continued delinquency blocks issuance of the Paz y Salvo tax-clearance certificate, prevents notarial registration of foundation amendments, and failure to pay for three consecutive years causes administrative strike-off and dissolution through the Public Registry of Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Sworn Declaration and Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, under Law 70 of 2019 and DGI Resolution 2020-0034
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 30 (within 30 days after the December 31 fiscal year-end); any transfer, pledge, or replacement of foundation beneficiary rights must additionally be reported within 30 days of the notarial act or written foundation-council resolution, whichever first occurs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines against the foundation and the Panamanian resident registered agent up to USD 5,000 per violation; suspension of tax-clearance certifications and registered-agent services; wilful concealment or false declarations escalate to the AML/CFT sanctioning regime of Law 23 of 2015, including higher monetary penalties and potential criminal liability for the responsible agent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is compulsory for a Panama Private Interest Foundation whose tug-towage and emergency maritime salvage contracts are executed wholly outside Panamanian territorial waters and generate no Panama-source income. A mandatory independent audit by a Panamanian-licensed CPA arises only where the foundation (i) develops taxable commercial activity physically or economically located in Panama, (ii) is designated a Gran Contribuyente by DGI, or (iii) records Panama-source gross income above the DGI statutory certification threshold of approximately USD 500,000 per annum.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS or IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para Pymes) as authorized by Panama's accounting standards mandate under Law 57 of 1978; the Foundation Charter or Regulations may validly direct the Foundation Council to maintain a cash-basis internal accounting record for non-statutory operational purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident registered agent must file the DGI UBO sworn declaration annually by January 30 and update it within 30 days after any transfer of beneficiary rights, variation of the endowment, change of Foundation Council members, or appointment of a protector. The agent's compliance duty is continuing: before processing the annual franchise tax payment, the agent must obtain and archive the notarized foundation-council minutes documenting the owner and beneficiary structure for the reporting year and cross-check the declared UBO file against the Foundation Charter, Regulations, and private foundation registers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro del Consejo de la Fundación)
Register of Beneficiaries and Founder (Registro de Beneficiarios y Fundador)
Register of Foundation Assets and Endowment (Registro del Patrimonio Fundacional)
Foundation Council Minute Book (Libro de Actas del Consejo de la Fundación)
Register of Protector and Contractual Third-Party Appointees (Registro de Protector y Apoderados)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 – USD 1,800 per annum (Panama licensed attorney or professional corporate agent; covers registered office, statutory-register custody in Spanish, DGI franchise-tax payment handling, UBO platform updates, and routine notarial formalities)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 4,000 per annum (voluntary Panamanian CPA review or financial-oversight engagement; payable only if audit is elected under the Foundation Charter or a Panama-source activity threshold is crossed)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on taxable Panama-source net income for ordinary corporate taxpayers. A Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is not subject to corporate income tax on non-Panama-source income; it instead pays a flat annual tax of USD 350.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation excludes foreign-source income derived from offshore towage and salvage operations performed outside Panama. The PIF structure benefits from the USD 350 annual flat tax in lieu of net-income CIT. No additional tax holiday applies to this marine salvage and towage scope.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1083 – Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas, filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; quarterly advance tax declarations are also required for entities with active Panama-source economic activity.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than three months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the filing deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, RUC number, and fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PIF's RUC as issued by the DGI and state the fiscal period. Non-resident status does not eliminate the filing obligation where Panama-source income exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived from activities performed, assets located, or rights used within Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Panama-source towing and salvage revenues. Exclude all revenue from offshore operations performed entirely outside Panamanian territory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from sources outside Panama that is excluded under the territorial regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source maritime salvage and towage income must be fully disclosed on this exclusion line, supported by voyage logs, casualty contracts, and evidence of performance outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses attributable exclusively to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions supported by invoices, crew payroll, fuel costs, and insurance premiums related to Panama-source revenue. Allocate shared costs using a consistent and documented basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 – Tax Credits and Advance Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments and creditable withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply quarterly advance declarations and any withholding certificates obtained from Panamanian payors. No foreign tax credit is available for non-Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Final Box – Net Tax Due or Balance in Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting tax liability after deductions, credits, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF with only exempt foreign-source income, enter zero net tax due. If Panama-source commercial activity exists, the 25% rate applies to the taxable base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty of 10% of the tax payable, plus monthly interest surcharges of 1% per month or fraction on the overdue amount; a daily monetary correction is not separately levied but the monthly surcharge compounds. For returns with no tax payable, administrative fines range from USD 100 to USD 500 for small taxpayers and up to USD 10,000 for major contributors. Non-compliance also blocks the issuance of tax clearance certificates and may trigger automatic fiscal audits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on distributions characterized as dividends paid out of Panama-source retained earnings of an ordinary corporation. For a Private Interest Foundation, distributions to beneficiaries are generally foundation allocations or bequests and are not characterized as dividends where the distributed assets derive from non-Panama-source income. If a PIF engages in Panama-source commercial activity and distributes those profits, the 10% dividend withholding tax may apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Panama double taxation agreement, the beneficial owner must obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate from the DGI, endorsed by the PIF's registered agent, and present it to the withholding agent before payment, together with any treaty-specific claim form and, where required, a Form 990 exemption/refund request. The claimant must evidence economic substance, beneficial ownership, and compliance with limitation-of-benefits clauses. Panama's DTAs do not apply automatically; domestic withholding is applied at source unless the treaty explicitly provides for direct-source relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: Panama-source royalties paid to non-residents are subject to a 10% final withholding tax; Panama-source interest paid to non-residents is subject to a 5% withholding tax, subject to exemptions for certain international banking and export financing arrangements. Under active Panamanian DTAs, interest withholding may be reduced to 0%–10% and royalty withholding to 5%–10%, conditioned on tax residence, beneficial ownership, and substantive activity in the treaty partner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 250,000 – Mandatory Local File and contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Study required when related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000 in a fiscal year. Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds USD 50,000,000. Country-by-Country reporting is triggered at consolidated group turnover above USD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but economic substance and effective management are required to establish Panamanian tax residence, obtain treaty benefits, and avoid substance-over-form recharacterization. A PIF deriving offshore towage and salvage income must maintain a registered office, minutes of the Foundation Council, vessel charter or salvage contracts, voyage records, bank accounts, and an actual administrative presence in Panama where treaty residence is claimed. A paper-only foundation engaged in invoice routing is vulnerable to GAAR, tax evasion classification, and AML enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Willful Omission in CIT Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting Panama-source towing or salvage revenue from Formulario 1083, artificially shifting profit through related-party billing, or destroying AIS records, voyage logs, and casualty reports to reduce the Panama-source tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Panama Tax Code and Criminal Code, evasion is punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines up to three times the evaded tax; the DGI may re-determine income using indirect methods and apply the 25% CIT with monthly interest surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members who sign false returns or benefit from the diverted profit are jointly and severally liable for evaded taxes and penalties; travel bans, asset seizures, civil restitution, and disqualification from serving as directors in Panama may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF to receive salvage escrow proceeds from fictitious casualties, layering funds through related towage companies, commingling foundation assets with third-party illegal proceeds, or conducting cash-based towage settlements without beneficial ownership identification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 and Criminal Code Articles 254–256 impose imprisonment of 5 to 15 years, administrative fines by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero of up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, and mandatory asset freezing and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members who knowingly accept or conceal tainted funds face criminal liability, joint civil restitution, travel restrictions, provisional embargoes, and revocation of professional licenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the transfer pricing affidavit or to maintain a Local File when intercompany fees for tug hire, salvage management services, or ocean towage allocations exceed USD 250,000, or using non-arm's-length tariff schedules to erode taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may adjust Panama-source income to arm's length, apply the 25% CIT on the adjustment, and impose penalties of up to 1% of the adjusted transaction value or USD 50,000, whichever is higher; NOL benefits may be recalculated or denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve deficient transfer pricing documentation may be assessed personally for resulting penalties under negligent management duties; denial or revocation of the tax residence certificate may trigger cross-border collection and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance in PIF
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal PIF with no physical office, no independent bank account, no Foundation Council minutes, and no operational records of the purported towage/salvage business, while routing revenue from salvage contracts through the foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI can disregard the PIF under substance-over-form principles, attribute the underlying towage/salvage profit to the beneficial owners, impose Panama CIT at 25%, and revoke the foundation's registration for non-payment or administrative non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the foundation veil subjects Foundation Council members and beneficial owners to civil restitution, joint liability for unpaid CIT and penalties, travel bans during fraud investigations, and imprisonment for wilful use of a sham legal vehicle.
